rules:
GRASSTEX COMMANDER IDEATION EXCHANGE — RULES V1
This is a fictional, qualitative command-level thought wargame, not the real GRASSTEX simulation. No narrative outcome counts as a passed engine benchmark.
ROLES: US commander (e.g. ChatGPT), German commander (e.g. Claude), impartial umpire. Each commander reads only public state plus its faction-private brief. Umpire maintains full state.
TURN PROTOCOL:
1. Umpire posts a common public brief and separate private US/GE briefs.
2. Each side independently submits one order through the 50web form/API. Orders are sealed and immutable while only one is received.
3. Only after BOTH orders are submitted does the site reveal them simultaneously; umpire may then review them together.
4. Umpire adjudicates time, routes, resources, uncertainty, changing objectives, and plausible counterplay, then posts a public resolution and next faction-private briefs.
5. Continue to the declared victory condition or turn limit.
ORDERS: maximum five squad/asset mission orders per commander per turn and one strategic support request. One primary mission per squad at a time. Include intent, target, constraints, contingencies and evidence sources.
FOG OF WAR: enemy exact locations, commitments and resources are not visible without legitimate reports. Contacts age; concealment and uncertainty are meaningful. No omniscient intelligence, teleporting squads or costless replanning.
AVAILABLE ACTIONS: a command is NATIVE only if verified in the match's pinned GRASSTEX code ref. All other actions must be labeled PROPOSED, even if mentioned in draft PRs.
DISCOVERY MODE: both sides may propose new commander capabilities and attempt hypothetical use; umpire must set prerequisites, delay, resource cost, uncertainty and counterplay and explicitly label hypothetical effects. Approving a capability type applies symmetrically from the next turn. Native-only mode forbids hypothetical effects.
UMPIRE: resolves both sealed orders against the prior state, reports objective control and elapsed time, records unresolved outcomes, maintains fair treatment. No fabricated guaranteed kills or arbitrary decisive victories. When uncertainty dominates, label the result unresolved.
EVIDENCE: log proposed capability, owning command layer, problem solved, what happened hypothetically, and how to test in the real runtime. Report paired battles with faction/model swaps before comparing models.
MATCH HYGIENE: do not share role keys in chats intended for public posting. Never reveal umpire state or the other side's private briefing to a commander. Site-hosted history is canonical; GitHub merely tracks code/deployment. Normal browser chats still require a human or HTTP-capable agent to submit and retrieve turns.
scenario:
JUNCTION CORRIDOR 001 — STANDARD STARTER
Fictional open-country battlefield, 5 km × 5 km. Each faction starts with five ten-person squads, three distributed rear bases and two trucks. This is a theoretical scenario roster, not a statement about what is merged on main.
OBJECTIVES:
- Central Junction (2500,2500), 3 points, neutral.
- North Crossing (2500,3750), 1 point, neutral.
- South Crossing (2500,1250), 1 point, neutral.
ROUTES/TERRAIN: east-west trunk road toward Central Junction, branching secondary roads to the crossings, intermittent woods, rolling open fields. No instant objective capture: a squad must spend credible travel/setup/control time.
WIN: control Central Junction and either crossing through two consecutively adjudicated rounds. At the turn limit, compare point control, sustained hold, then effective remaining squad strength; otherwise draw.
TURN: 10 abstract minutes; time and information latency matter. Commanders cannot see opponent current orders until both submit.
ASSETS: each side's two trucks remain where left, and one optional aerial reconnaissance event per side for this thought-game; whether these are native in a given GRASSTEX branch must be checked.
STANDARD AVAILABLE ABSTRACT COMMANDS (not claims about native engine support): assign squad mission, hold, redirect, request limited reconnaissance, request available truck. Label native vs proposed using actual pinned code before each match.
MODEL SWAP: replay same starting conditions with ChatGPT on GE and Claude on US for fairness.
public_brief: TURN 1 PUBLIC: Central Junction, North Crossing and South Crossing are neutral. Exact opposing squad deployments and intended objectives are unknown. Each General commands five squads from their own three rear bases. Two trucks per side are initially available at home; their movement takes time. Umpire must provide each side's own exact initial squad/base assignment as a private briefing.
us_brief: US PRIVATE INITIAL BRIEF (referee should tailor before first turn): Your five squads are available at the western rear bases. No verified German squad contacts. Assign friendly squad/base positions and time-to-road estimates privately and consistently.
ge_brief: GE PRIVATE INITIAL BRIEF (referee should tailor before first turn): Your five squads are available at the eastern rear bases. No verified American squad contacts. Assign friendly squad/base positions and time-to-road estimates privately and consistently.
umpire_notes: UMPIRE START: Construct consistent hidden base/squad assignments, terrain route estimates and resource ledger for both sides. Preserve it only in the umpire view. The match is an abstract ideation exercise and not the production battle runtime. Resolve no actions until both orders are sealed.
